stats.label: AI use cases coached to production

caseStudies.name: Anomaly detection as a reusable capability
caseStudies.role: Owner of the deployment approach and coach to site project teams; sites built and ran their own projects.
caseStudies.problem: A critical gear failure on a mill showed that degradation was visible in the data long before it became a breakdown — but every site was building detection from scratch.
caseStudies.action: Standardised anomaly-detection deployment on SmartBox edge infrastructure, Siemens Industrial Edge and historian data, and coached 20+ projects across Asia, Europe and the Americas.
caseStudies.result: Early detection of mill degradation became the reference case and is now the template for predictive maintenance across the network.
caseStudies.learning: Scale comes from the deployment pattern, not the model. A boring, repeatable pipeline beats a clever one-off.

caseStudies.name: Touchless quality: replacing manual sampling
caseStudies.role: Set up the ML approach and led alignment with the quality organisation, delivered with site and data teams.
caseStudies.problem: Product quality was checked through manual sampling — slow, labour-intensive and blind between samples.
caseStudies.action: Established a cloud ML approach for continuous quality prediction and worked with the quality organisation on validation and acceptance criteria.
caseStudies.result: Secured quality-organisation acceptance for scale-up, with ~$12M of identified opportunity across further lines.
caseStudies.learning: In regulated domains the hardest part is trust. Bring the quality team in at the start, not at sign-off.

caseStudies.name: WISE Coach Qualification (WCQ) program
caseStudies.role: Global program lead: content, coaching frameworks and session facilitation.
caseStudies.problem: AI training was happening, but it rarely turned into deployed solutions on the plant floor.
caseStudies.action: Lead the global WCQ program: learning journeys, coaching frameworks, global sessions and cross-site communities of practice, each tied to a real use case. Created AI-X templates so engineers can build and deploy AI without deep data-science support.
caseStudies.result: Turned training into a capability engine — 55+ coached use cases across 11+ business units, with self-serve AI patterns adopted in 6 business units.
caseStudies.learning: Learning sticks when it ships. Tie every cohort to a production problem with an owner.

caseStudies.name: RapidMLOps: ML from Excel-like tools to the PLC
caseStudies.metricLabel: PLC vendor families supported (Siemens, Rockwell, Mitsubishi)
caseStudies.role: Designed and built the framework as my master thesis and led the production-line pilot.
caseStudies.problem: Engineers built good models in JMP, but there was no path to run them on edge devices against live PLC data.
caseStudies.action: Built an end-to-end framework to package, deploy and manage models with Azure ML, GitHub and Power Apps; enabled JMP models on Siemens edge devices with real-time S7 PLC read/write, and a generic method for Siemens, Rockwell and Mitsubishi PLCs via OPC UA, MQTT, ZMQ and EtherNet/IP.
caseStudies.result: Piloted on a production line with millisecond predictions for closed-loop control; built a lab test stand (pH soft sensor) and trained professionals from multiple business units.
caseStudies.learning: Meet engineers in the tools they already use, then automate everything after the model.

caseStudies.name: AI-X Removing Entry Barrier
caseStudies.role: Developed a CI/CD pipeline for packaging my python language based ML models for edge deployment .
caseStudies.problem:
The effort of packaging model is equal to deploying model.
Mostly people somehow develop ML model for production but the journey to deploy takes equal time intensive. Mostly , we have siemens industrial edge and to deploy on to it, there is SDK which you adapt to your model to run on the edge. I took the SDK and found where the areas that changes and what is it needed to adapt. Took the info created a skeleton that can fit any ML model through simple text inputs to the workflow and github action based on the input produces the final deployment package. 

It has a lot of pytest and unit test and has standard pipelines for quality check of all models for pre processing and post processing.

Integrated it with Sonarcube for IT checks and application rejestration and standard structure for testing timely on performance and check on usage and reception of the tool. It is now a fully stable solution used for pacakging most of the models which are being deployed on the edge.

caseStudyNote: Dollar values are rounded estimates from internal business cases, not audited savings. "Identified opportunity" means potential value across further sites, not realised value. Results are team outcomes; my role is stated on each case. Details are kept at a level that respects confidentiality.

featuredProject.name: Coinfluence
featuredProject.summary: A personal finance dashboard I designed and built for my household. It reads monthly exports from six German banks and brokers and answers three questions: how much did we spend, how much did we save and invest, and who owes whom on the shared card.
features: One upload for every bank: the account is detected and duplicates are skipped
Swipe deck to split shared credit-card charges, with a settle-up checklist
Budgets, recurring-payment detection and net worth over time
Two profiles with separate data and settings

decisions.title: Local-first by design
decisions.text: Financial data never leaves the laptop; sync goes only to a private repo, and the sync script refuses to run on a public one.

decisions.title: Trust over features
decisions.text: Automatic backups before every save, file locking, and damaged files are never overwritten.

decisions.title: Tested without real data
decisions.text: The test suite builds fake statements for every bank, and CI runs it on every push.

featuredProject.note: The source is private because it handles personal financial data. Happy to demo it live.

aboutMe:
I was a 90s kid who grew up watching science fiction, fascinated by worlds where technology could do things that seemed impossible. I’ve always loved the idea of what could be—and the curiosity to figure out how to make it happen. Looking back, perhaps it’s no surprise that I found my way into IT, AI, and innovation. Today, I get to bring a little of that futuristic thinking into the real world.

At Procter & Gamble’s Kronberg Innovation Center, I lead the scaling of manufacturing AI across a global plant network—connecting factory-floor challenges with data science, IT, and engineering to turn promising pilots into solutions that work in production.

I’m fascinated by the technology, but even more by what makes innovation stick: solving the right problems, building reusable solutions, bringing cross-functional teams together, and empowering people to carry ideas forward themselves.

Beyond technology, I’m a curious lifelong learner who enjoys teaching, building teams, and turning ambitious goals into tangible results.

I’m a planner with a bias for action. I like turning ideas into plans and plans into progress. But life rarely follows a perfect roadmap. When things don’t go to plan, I adapt, learn, and keep moving. I’m an optimist about detours; sometimes, what feels like a setback leads somewhere even better than we had imagined.

I’m also a strategic thinker who likes to roll up my sleeves and get things done. I enjoy seeing the bigger picture while figuring out the practical steps to make it happen. And I believe the best ideas rarely succeed in isolation—they need people who challenge one another, share knowledge, and bring out the best in each other. For me, that’s where strategy turns into progress: when good ideas meet good people and the willingness to make things happen.
